The acknowledged expansion therefore does not establish the promised narrow/public runtime command boundary and can leak Ledger Query responsibility if later registered. Replace the alias with a narrow wrapper that returns exactly finding_runtime_evidence_run and finding_runtime_evidence_verify and wire/export the intended boundary, or remove the public-boundary promise/expansion with proof that the direct registered ledger handler is the canonical contract.

packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:569 display-ID allocation still uses findings.length + 1, so a sparse legacy set such as F-001/F-003 allocates F-003 again; lines 632-634 then find the old row by display ID and neither replace nor append when recordId differs, silently hiding the newly durable ledger record from readFindings. This preserves the historical ID-reuse/vanishing-row failure despite globally unique recordIds.

packages/main/src/core/store.ts:486-499 overwrites a matching findings.json row with the original append-only ledger finding payload whenever recordId matches. finding_resolve only updates findings.json at handlers/finding.ts:821-843 and appends no ledger status mutation. At HEAD 591642d, commits e93c480 and 591642d are finding_resolve metadata commits, yet proof-or-stop finding_list --storyId=B-fe8f --json still returns F-001 and F-002 status=open. Thus resolution/dismissal is reverted on read, making user output and lifecycle consumers observe stale open state and invalidating exactly-once historical correction. Add append-only status-transition records/current projection plus a regression that resolves and rereads a ledger-backed Finding.

packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:821-843 — finding_resolve still mutates only the findings.json compatibility mirror via readFindings/writeFindings and never appends a fenced ledger status-transition/successor record. The repository itself now demonstrates the lost update: commit e93c480257 resolves F-001, then commit 591642d288 resolves F-002 while reverting F-001 from resolved back to open; current finding_list confirms F-001 is open. This violates Story 3 objective that every Finding-system mutation be durable/exactly-once and lets concurrent closeouts resurrect a gate-consumed finding. Route resolve/dismiss status transitions through one append-only, idempotent fenced ledger transaction, derive the compatibility projection from the ledger, and add a concurrent two-finding resolve regression proving both resolutions survive and replay returns the original transition IDs.

packages/main/src/handlers/transition-orchestrator.ts:131-155 — the new dependency gate releases a prerequisite solely when dependency.phase === DONE; it never proves the dependency branch is merged into local main/current baseline. packages/main/src/core/partial-done-recovery.ts:123-151 explicitly models the real failure state phase=DONE while story/<id> is not an ancestor of main, so phase alone is not the accepted DONE-and-merged contract. The smoke fixture compounds this by directly writeStory(... phase:DONE) and calling the dependency released, which cannot prove merged-state behavior. A partial-DONE dependency can therefore authorize dependent DEV before its APIs exist on main. Fail closed on both canonical DONE and a mechanical merge/ancestry (or equivalent signed merged-capability) proof, and mutate the merge fact independently in the dependency regression.

packages/main/src/handlers/finding-ledger.ts:632-858 / current B-fe8f ledger — the delivered public query does not work against the Story that produced it: `proof-or-stop finding_ledger_query --storyId=B-fe8f` on current HEAD fails closed with `finding-ledger-query:ledger_receipt_unsigned`. CHK-005 promises a stable signed query for ledger/CAS/idempotency/runtime/migration inputs and Story 2 depends on that public port; an unreadable canonical ledger cannot satisfy it. Add a bounded append-only migration/legacy-binding path (without rewriting committed semantic bytes), prove the current real B-fe8f ledger becomes queryable, and retain negative rejection for genuinely unsigned/tampered post-migration rows.

packages/main/src/handlers/finding-ledger.ts:386-417,432-481 validates only the proposal top-level key set and shallow variant shape. It never requires FindingRef.recordId, the required dependencyBundle members, non-empty current witness receipts, or a truthful proposalSigner algorithm/keyId/trustRoot; receipt currentness rejects only the explicit boolean false, so an omitted result is accepted. Repro after rebuilding dist: a correctly Ed25519-signed proposal with findingRef missing recordId, dependencyBundle={}, currentWitness.receiptIds=[], and proposalSigner.algorithm="rsa"/empty keyId/trustRoot returns {valid:true}. This contradicts the immutable exact-union, named signer/trust, dependency-bundle, and non-current-receipt fail-closed contract.

packages/main/src/handlers/finding-ledger.ts:886-927,1107-1124,1131-1147,1232-1251 derives both the runtime signer and its fresh key status solely from the same invocation environment. A caller can generate a new keypair, set PROOF_OR_STOP_RUNTIME_EVIDENCE_PRIVATE_KEY/PUBLIC_KEY, mint a receipt, and have that same unpersisted key treated as current; it can also omit the caller-controlled revoked-key env to remove revocation. finding_ledger_query additionally accepts caller-supplied trustedKeys. The production smoke itself generates a fresh key at tasks/finding-ledger-runtime-smoke.ts:808-838 and immediately persists a valid receipt, proving there is no independent repository trust/rotation registry. This makes signer freshness and revocation self-asserted rather than verifier-derived.

packages/main/src/core/evidence/artifact-store.ts:59-66,83-103 performs realpath containment once, then reuses the unresolved logical dir for exists/read, openSync(temp), renameSync(destination), and directory fsync. There is no held directory descriptor, no no-follow/openat-style operation, and no lock covering the containment check through publication. A local symlink/directory swap after line 85 therefore makes the later path components resolve outside the project even though the initial check passed; the current smoke at tasks/finding-ledger-runtime-smoke.ts:1134-1148 covers only a symlink already present before the check. payload.desc: core/store.ts:1113,1129 with core/finding-ledger.ts:78-82: readFindings hard-fails when the Finding ledger trust key is unavailable, and that key never travels with the repository. findingLedgerKeyPath resolves the ed25519 key under gitCommonDir, i.e. inside .git, which git clone never copies, while git ls-files --error-unmatch confirms .proof-or-stop/story/actives/B-fe8f/finding-ledger.json IS tracked and does travel. store.ts:1113 loads trust via the non-creating currentFindingLedgerTrustFromWorkspace; store.ts:368 returns undefined for every carrier when trust is undefined; trustedLegacyBaseFindingCarrier also yields undefined because its inner binding lookup uses the same helper; store.ts:1129 then throws FINDING_LEDGER_AUTHORITY_INVALID on the first base finding record. A clone that creates its own key gets a different keyId and trustRootDigest, so verifyFindingLedgerReceipt fails identically. Consequence: in any clone other than the one that wrote the ledger, readFindings on a ledger-bearing Story throws instead of degrading, breaking finding_list, signature_backfill over listStoryIds, and the readFindings projection that process-fact-registry registers as a canPassReview gate consumer. Before commit 845023258f base Finding payloads were projected without trust, so the same clone still read them; this is a regression introduced by that repair. It also runs against execution-plan acceptance line 3618 that legacy Findings remain readable without bulk rewrite. Protected surfaces: lifecycle_gate, cli_primary_entrypoint, historical_evidence_integrity. Coverage gap: no regression exercises a ledger that HAS base finding records while the key is absent; runReadOnlyColdStartRegression only asserts finding_ledger_query and finding_runtime_evidence_verify refusals on an empty fixture, and runBaseFindingAuthorityRegression always has the key present. Severity: high.
payload.uncertaintyReason: Source-verified but not executed end to end. Verified by source reading plus git: the ledger file is tracked (git ls-files --error-unmatch succeeded), the key path resolves under git rev-parse --git-common-dir which is the untracked .git directory, and the store.ts path from undefined trust to the throw is unconditional. NOT executed: this session was denied every filesystem-writing probe (mkdir, cp, heredoc, node inline module), so I could not run readFindings against a copy of the real ledger under a keyless git root. I also did not exhaustively exclude a mitigation outside the files I read, such as a DONE-time exclusion of finding-ledger.json, a rebinding migration on first read in a new clone, or a policy that ledger-bearing Stories are never read from another clone. Owner reproduction: copy finding-ledger.json and findings.json plus a minimal proof-or-stop.config.json into a fresh git init directory, then call StoryStore(root).readFindings on B-fe8f via packages/main/dist/core/store.js and expect FINDING_LEDGER_AUTHORITY_INVALID. If it reproduces this becomes verified high and should block REVIEW.

payload.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/done-required-validation-smoke.ts:381 (new in the F-050 repair) builds the retired brand prefix as an expression, ['LAT','TICE_'].join(''), rather than a literal. I verified with grep that the file now contains zero literal occurrences of that retired token, so the only construction is the runtime concatenation. The surrounding assertion logic is correct and matches F-050's required repair: it asserts retired ambient spellings remain semantic while canonical spellings stay session-neutral, without restoring obsolete aliases or weakening the digest assertion. The concern is narrower and is about readability and gate visibility: the line carries no comment explaining why the prefix is assembled instead of written, so a future maintainer cannot tell whether this is deliberate residue-policy compliance or accidental obfuscation, and any literal-token residue scan over this file cannot see the token it is reasoning about. CLAUDE.md documents a sanctioned route for legitimately retaining historical brand tokens, namely the identity-cutover verifier's per-file per-token rules, which would make the exception explicit and auditable instead of invisible. Suggested bounded fix: keep the same behavior and either add a one-line comment naming the residue-policy reason, or register the literal through the sanctioned per-token mechanism. Severity: low.
payload.uncertaintyReason: The mechanical facts are verified: the concatenation exists at that line and the file contains zero literal occurrences of the retired token. What I cannot determine from the sources I read is which residue-policy reading governs. If the policy means no new literal retired tokens may appear in product runtime source, this construction complies and only the missing explanatory comment remains. If the policy means retained historical tokens must be registered with the identity-cutover verifier's per-file per-token rules, this bypasses that registration. I did not read the residue verifier implementation or scripts/verify-proof-or-stop-residue.mjs to settle which reading applies, and I ran no test, so I am not asserting a policy violation. Filed low and suspected so it is preserved and traceable without blocking; it is non-blocking under any reading and does not affect the ledger work.
